items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1961-06-21
items.q: And I wrote to Kennedy, who had gone to New York and was in New York, and asked him when, when he arranged that tune.

ctx.x: The music as well as the words?

The music and words. And this was about 1904 and 1905 that I heard, heard him play that. And I had heard my, I heard the office boy that, that sang these fragments of blues. I'd heard him sing little parts of that. Oh, my honey baby, she can cook and stew. She's a good doing baby through and through, but she's got low down ways. And something of that sort, you know. But just little fragments that this office boy sang. But anyhow, in 1906, Kennedy gave a concert in Algiers. And he played the piano and his niece…
Honey Baby. As you remember, it was the familiar blues chords.
